transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. Um, well, I guess I'm just here because... I've been having these thoughts lately. It's probably nothing major, really, just some stress from work. I'm a designer, so I have to be detail-oriented, but lately I keep getting these nagging thoughts that I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or maybe sent the wrong version of a file to a client. 

Even when I look at it and I can see it’s fine—like, perfectly fine—my mind just keeps circling back to it. It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I know I'm good at my job. I just... I can't seem to turn it off. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking things over and over, or mentally going through certain steps—to try to ease the worry or make sure everything is perfect?

Um... yeah, I guess I do a little bit of that. It's not, like, a huge problem or anything, just a little quirk I've picked up. 

Before I submit a project now, I'll usually re-open the file... just to be absolutely sure, you know? And I'll compare the layers again, re-save it... and sometimes I just sort of mentally walk through every single design choice I made, just one more time. It doesn't take over my whole day or anything dramatic! It just... maybe makes me a little slower than I used to be. And maybe a bit less free creatively, because I'm so focused on not messing up. 

Is that... is that normal for someone in a creative field? I really try not to let it affect my work too much. I hope that's the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do these thoughts or the need to check things interfere with your daily life or cause you a lot of distress, even if you try to ignore or suppress them?

Um... distress? I mean, I wouldn't say it's *distress*, exactly. I'm still getting all my work done, I promise! I haven't let any clients down or anything like that. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, I have been missing a few of our internal deadlines lately. Just the soft deadlines with my team, not the final ones! It's just because I need that extra time to double-check everything. And... I suppose I have been playing it a bit safe with my designs recently. I used to pitch these really bold, out-of-the-box concepts, but now I find myself holding back. I just worry that if I try something too complicated, I might overlook a tiny detail and mess it up. 

I really want to move up to a creative director role soon, and I just... I don't want a silly mistake to ruin my chances, you know? So I guess it is affecting me a little bit, but I'm really trying to keep it under control. I'm sorry, I know I shouldn't be letting it get in the way of my career goals. Am I making a bigger deal out of this than I should be?
Do you ever have thoughts that come into your mind that you don’t want or that feel intrusive, like they don’t belong to you, and that really bother you or make you feel anxious?

Um... intrusive? I mean... I wouldn't say they don't belong to me. They're just my own worries, really. It's just like I mentioned before, um, I get these nagging thoughts about my work. 

It's just that fear that I've missed a tiny mistake in a layout, or maybe that I attached the wrong version of a file in an email to a client. And... even when I look at the screen and I can see that it's probably completely fine, my mind just... keeps circling back to it. It just loops. It's a little annoying, I guess, but it's not like crazy thoughts or anything bad! Just... just work stuff. I hope that's okay? Like, I'm not crazy for having those kinds of thoughts, right? It's just because I care about doing a good job.
Do you feel like you have to perform certain actions or mental steps a specific number of times or in a certain way to prevent something bad from happening or to reduce your anxiety?

Um... well, I think that's sort of what I was trying to explain earlier? With my design files. I don't do things, like, a hundred times, I promise! But I do have that specific little routine. 

Like I mentioned, before I submit a project, I always re-open the file, compare the layers, re-save it... and then do that mental walk-through of all my design choices. I guess I do kind of have to do it in that exact order, just to feel... settled, you know? To make the worry stop so I can finally hit send. 

It really doesn't take over my whole day or anything extreme! It just... makes the whole process a little slower than it needs to be. And, like I said, it kind of keeps me from being as creatively free as I want to be, because I'm just sticking to this rigid little checking routine. 

Is that... does that answer your question? I hope it's okay that I brought the same example up again. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information... am I doing okay?

Even though you said it's not causing major problems, do these thoughts and checking behaviors ever make you feel really anxious or upset, especially if you're unable to complete your routine the way you want to?

Um... anxious? I mean... I wouldn't say *really* anxious. I'm usually pretty good at just... getting it done, you know? 

I guess... well, if someone interrupts me when I'm right in the middle of checking the layers, or if my computer freezes while I'm re-saving... I do get a little bit flustered. Just a tiny bit! Because then I feel like I have to start the whole mental walk-through over again, just to be absolutely sure. And if I can't do it right then, like if I have to run to a meeting... it does kind of sit in the back of my mind. It just feels a little uncomfortable, like an itch I can't scratch, until I can get back to my desk and finish it properly. 

But it's not like I'm having a breakdown over it or anything! I try really hard not to let anyone see that it bothers me. I just take a deep breath and deal with it. I hope that doesn't sound too silly? I know it's probably just me being a perfectionist... I'm answering these questions okay, right?
Do you ever perform any actions or mental rituals outside of your work-related checking routine to try to reduce anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Um... outside of work? No, I don't... I really don't think so. 

I mean, I like to keep my apartment tidy, of course, but just... normal neat, you know? Not like a strict routine or anything like that. It really is just that one specific thing with my design files at the office. Once I log off for the day, I'm actually pretty relaxed! I just read or watch TV like anyone else. 

I hope that's not... I mean, is it okay if it's just that one work thing? I know you're asking all these questions to get a full picture, and I don't want to be unhelpful by not having more to tell you. But I really can't think of anything else in my personal life. I'm doing this right, aren't I? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

Have you ever had upsetting thoughts that keep coming into your mind, even when you try not to think about them—like worries about harming someone, strange violent images, or thoughts that go against your values?

Oh, gosh, no. Nothing like that. 

I mean... violent images or harming someone? No, definitely not. That sounds really awful, and I... I don't have anything like that happening in my head. My worries are really just about, you know, making a mistake on a project or messing up a file. Just normal work stress things, really. Nothing dark or against my values at all. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have those kinds of thoughts? I know you have to ask to make sure, but I promise I'm completely fine in that department. I'm really just a normal person who gets a little too hung up on saving her work properly. That's... that's an okay answer, right? I'm not leaving anything important out?
Have you ever felt that these thoughts or checking behaviors are excessive or unreasonable, even if they’re mostly limited to your work routine?

Excessive? Um... I don't know if I'd use the word *excessive*. I mean, maybe a little bit unnecessary sometimes? 

Like, logically, I know the computer probably saved it the first time. I know that. But... I don't think it's completely unreasonable to just want to be thorough, you know? In my line of work, a corrupted file can mean hours of lost progress, so... it's just being careful. Maybe a tiny bit overly careful? But not... not crazy or completely out of bounds. 

I mean, I definitely don't think it's a huge problem. It's just a little quirk I have. I really hope I don't sound like I'm making excuses or anything! I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea about it. It's not taking over my life or anything like that. That makes sense, right? I'm explaining it okay?

Outside of work, do your thoughts or checking behaviors ever cause you noticeable distress or interfere with your ability to function in other areas of your life, like with relationships, hobbies, or daily tasks?

Um, outside of work? No, definitely not. Like I said, when I'm home, I'm just relaxing. It doesn't get in the way of my friends or anything like that. I'm completely fine there.

I mean... I guess if I'm being completely honest, maybe it does affect things at the office a *tiny* bit more than I made it sound? Like, I'm still getting all my work done, I promise! I'm a good employee. But... I have been missing a few of my own internal deadlines lately because I'm just double-checking things so much. And... well, I've sort of stopped pitching my bolder design ideas. I just get so worried I'll overlook some small detail and ruin it, and I really want to be considered for a creative director role someday, so I don't want to mess up. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent! I'm still doing good work, really. It's just... maybe holding me back a little bit? Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits symptoms consistent with obsessive-compulsive disorder, primarily centered around intrusive, distressing thoughts related to work performance and a need to perform specific checking behaviors to reduce anxiety. These symptoms are limited to the workplace context and do not generalize to other areas of life, but they do result in mild functional impairment and distress when routines are interrupted.
